headline_marked: [[LPG crisis persists, prices remain high]] in Bangladesh; 12kg cylinders Tk 500-600 above BERC rate
headline: LPG crisis persists, prices remain high in Bangladesh; 12kg cylinders Tk 500-600 above BERC rate
summary: Despite recent price adjustments by BERC, the supply crisis for Liquid Petroleum Gas continues, with 12kg cylinders being sold at Tk 500-600 above the official rate across the market.
details: Despite the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) increasing and adjusting prices, the supply crisis for Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) has not abated. Distributors report that only six companies are regularly supplying, and even they cannot meet demand.

The most commonly used 12kg LPG cylinders in Bangladesh are still being sold for Tk 500 to Tk 600 more than the government-set price. For October, BERC set the maximum retail price for a 12kg cylinder at Tk 1,837, an increase from Tk 1,585 in September.

However, consumers are purchasing 12kg LPG cylinders for Tk 2,300 to Tk 2,500 in the market. The LP Gas Traders Welfare Association sent a letter to BERC on October 6, stating that LPG companies issued new price lists on the day of BERC's announcement, setting 12kg cylinder prices between Tk 1,740 and Tk 2,000.

The association cited increased fuel prices, license fees, and other ancillary costs as reasons why selling LPG at the BERC-determined price is not feasible. They detailed additional costs for transport, handling, and operational expenses, claiming a need for Tk 150 per cylinder at the distributor level.

Currently, distributors receive only Tk 50 commission per cylinder, leading to a Tk 100 deficit. This discrepancy, coupled with varying prices among companies, creates an unstable market situation, according to the association.

BERC, however, maintains that the wholesale price is Tk 1,742, and with a Tk 50 commission, distributors should sell to retailers for Tk 1,792. BERC Chairman Jalal Ahmed acknowledged receiving the association's letter but stated that cost adjustments require a public hearing.

He added that the commission would discuss the proposals in an upcoming meeting. BERC has been setting LPG prices since April 2021, and the Tk 50 commission for distributors was established at that time.

Consumers frequently complain that LPG is not sold at the regulated price, and supply shortages often lead to inflated prices, making it difficult to obtain LPG even at higher costs. A Mirpur resident reported paying Tk 2,500 for a 12kg cylinder recently, Tk 663 more than the government-set price.

Approximately one crore customers in Bangladesh use LPG, with 80% for domestic cooking. Demand has significantly increased since residential gas connections were halted in 2015, now exceeding 1.5 million tons annually. The sector is 99% private, relying on imports.

LPG is also used in industry and transport, where filling stations are experiencing supply shortages. The LPG Filling Station Owners Association reported receiving only 5-6 tons against a monthly demand of 30 tons per station, leading to losses.

Loab (LPG importers and suppliers association) stated that imports in August and September were normal, at 158,000 and 156,000 metric tons respectively, suggesting increased supply might take more time. Distributors claim some companies reduced supply from September 20, and if their demands are not met, they are considering stopping LPG sales.

headline: Bangladesh Police announces nationwide constable recruitment across 64 districts; apply until October 30
summary: The Bangladesh Police is seeking new personnel for 'Trainee Recruit Constable (TRC)' positions, aiming to strengthen law enforcement with a focus on discipline, security, and progress. The recruitment drive emphasizes "Service through Duty" and is open to elig
details: The Bangladesh Police has published a recruitment circular for 'Trainee Recruit Constable (TRC)' positions, aiming to bolster its force nationwide. This initiative, guided by the motto 'Discipline, Security, Progress' and the slogan 'Service through Duty,' seeks to recruit police members across the country.

AIG (Media and Public Relations) Kamarun Munira of Police Headquarters confirmed the publication of the constable recruitment circular. While the exact number of constables to be recruited is yet to be determined, eligible and interested candidates from all districts of Bangladesh are encouraged to apply.
Applications will be accepted online via Teletalk's designated website, starting from October 13, 2026, at 10:00 AM. The deadline for submitting applications is October 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM.

Applicants must be permanent citizens of Bangladesh and unmarried. The minimum educational qualification required is an SSC or equivalent examination with a GPA of at least 2.5. Candidates must be between 18 and 20 years of age.

Physical eligibility criteria include a minimum height of 5 feet 6 inches for general and other quota male candidates, and 5 feet 4 inches for male candidates from ethnic minorities and freedom fighter quotas. Female candidates require a minimum height of 5 feet 4 inches for general quotas and 5 feet 2 inches for special quotas. Vision must be 6/6 for all applicants.

Police Headquarters has issued strict instructions to ensure 100% merit, eligibility, and transparency in the recruitment process. Authorities have warned that any false, incorrect, or hidden information in the application will lead to immediate cancellation of candidacy or appointment.

Furthermore, legal and administrative action will be taken if any provided information is found to be untrue even after employment. Interested candidates are urged to carefully complete the application form and pay the prescribed fee within the stipulated time on the website.
After completing the online application, the application fee must be paid within 72 hours using a prepaid Teletalk SIM, utilizing the user ID received.
